content.title: Terry Crews' Wife Rebecca Reveals She Has Parkinson's Disease, and Symptoms Were First Dismissed as Anxiety
content.text: During the April 6 episode of TODAY, Rebecca King Crews, the wife of America's Got Talent Host Terry Crews, shared publicly for the first time that she has Parkinson's disease.How to WatchWatch TODAY weekdays at 7AM ET on NBC and Peacock.The 60-year-old, a singer and fashion designer, explained that her first symptoms appeared around 2012, which ultimately led to her diagnosis three years later.What is Parkinson's disease?According to the Mayo Clinic, "Parkinson's disease is a movement disorder of the nervous system that worsens over time. The nervous system is a network of nerve cells that controls many parts of the body, including movement." Early symptoms of the disease could include mild tremors in parts of the body, in one hand or a foot, or stiffness and slowing of movement.As the disease progresses, symptoms generally get worse.RELATED: Terry Crews' Wife Designed His America's Got Talent Finale SuitKing Crews said on TODAY that she first noticed something was wrong in 2012, when she had some slight numbness in her left foot. "And then my trainer noticed that my arm did not swing when I'd walk," she revealed. "And then I woke up one morning and my hand was shaking."Rebecca King Crews' Parkinson's disease initially attributed to "anxiety" by doctor King Crews said that she went to the doctor after her hand began shaking and was told, "Oh, you're having anxiety. You'll be fine." She asked for referrals to specialists just in case. "And it took three years to diagnose me," King Crews said. Crews, an actor, TV host, and former NFL player, told TODAY what his thoughts were when hearing for the first time that his wife had Parkinson's disease."Well, I knew she was a superhero," Crews said of his wife. "And she had already went through cancer and defeated it... This is why you get married... This is the battle that we were designed to fight together. And that's the whole way I see it. Where she's weak, I'm strong. Where I'm weak, she's strong. And we built each other up like that for almost 37 years and all the way to forever. That's how we're doing it."RELATED: Terry Crews Shares Rare, Gorgeous Photo From His 1989 Wedding to Wife RebeccaKing Crews also revealed on TODAY that she recently underwent an FDA-approved procedure — a bilateral focused ultrasound — to help with the symptoms on one side of her body. "I feel good," King Crews said of how she feels after that procedure. "I'm able to write my name and my dates, and I'm able to write with my right hand, for the first time in probably three years... So, I'm seeing improvement in my symptoms. I'm still in recovery. They say it's about three months of recovery. So, as you recover, you see more improvement."According to TODAY.com, the procedure involved the use of a device called Exablate Neuro to deliver ultrasound waves to specific areas on both sides of the brain, targeting areas related to the movement symptoms of Parkinson's disease. TODAY co-anchor Craig Melvin, who conducted the interview with the couple, explained to viewers that King Crews is scheduled to have "the second procedure in September, with the hope of treating the symptoms for the other side of [her] body." King Crews said that right now, her symptoms are improved on the one side of the body that was treated, but not the other. "So I'm looking forward to do the left side," she said. She added that she decided to come forward now with her diagnoses because initially, she didn't want people to feel sorry for her, but that now, "I really believe that this procedure and others like it are the new frontier of medicine. They were able to go into my brain without cutting me open."RELATED: Terry Crews Is So Sweet Blowing a Kiss to His Wife on the AGT Stage (VIDEO)King Crews said that she wanted to now share her story "just to give hope to people with Parkinson's because I believe that we're going to find a cure."Crews will return as host of AGT when Season 21 debuts this summer.Watch Terry and Rebecca Crew's April 6 TODAY appearance here.
